raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Apply canonical Miles deltas directly to live SGLang weights, including HF-base recovery on fresh engines. This targets upstream `main`; the `sglang-miles` counterpart is [SGLang #42210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42210), paired with [Miles #3894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3894).

## Modifications

- **Lifecycle/API:** `/get_gpu_delta_info`, `/update_weights_from_gpu_delta`, `/get_gpu_delta_status` and `/clear_gpu_delta_state` serve the Miles client. One update carries the negotiated participants/session and publication descriptor, then owns preparation, pause/fence/apply, all-rank acknowledgement and resume. Failed preparation is released; uncertain XOR application is never replayed. Model labels become visible before generation resumes.
- **Preparation:** validate manifests, read/hash into shared tmpfs, decode/copy into private rank HOST_NUMA arenas, and prepare byte descriptors and three fixed access-family kernels. Bulk byte copies release the GIL. Private scalar patches use empty storage for full replacement or a clone for partial replacement, with batched copies. Cache one decode-status kernel per device. Live weight writes wait for pause; concurrent-serving impact has not been measured. `GPU_DELTA_HOST_CACHE_DIR` must name host-shared tmpfs when overridden.
- **Apply/storage:** one hardware-DE stream, one Triton stream and exactly two decoded slots, ordered by decode-ready/apply-finished events. Sticky status guards subsequent mutation. DE-facing allocations own their CUDA storage; streams drain before release on failure/cancellation. No pipeline-depth tuning, runtime autotuning or encoded-HBM ring.
- **Integrity/recovery:** `validate_payload_hash=True` is the sole receiver hash-policy input; disabling it skips payload SHA passes only. Manifest/file/native checks remain. Ordinary updates use consecutive transport versions; fresh engines can accept HF base→current. State stays cached unless cleared explicitly or via `release_state=True` after successful resume. Cleanup does not change weights/version/pause timing; caller-owned pauses are preserved.
- **Observability:** retain rank/engine phase metrics for Miles/W&B without added collective, polling or device synchronization. Standard `SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1` marks host preparation, scheduler and worker/enqueue ranges; the benchmark controls capture. Disabled tracing leaves callables unchanged.

### Compatibility

Blackwell hardware DE; no software-decompression fallback or weight requantization. Admission maps existing FlashInfer packed buffers into canonical affine byte views; padding is excluded, aliases receive one XOR, and independently owned consumer images each receive it. There is no update-time weight/mask permutation.

| Weight format | FlashInfer TRTLLM family | CuTe DSL | MegaMoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | Yes | — | — |
| FP8 128×128, UE8M0 scales | Yes | — | — |
| MXFP8 | Yes | — | Yes |
| MXFP4 × MXFP8 activation | Yes | — | Yes |
| NVFP4 | W4A4 | W4A4 / W4A16 | W4A4 / W4A16 |

These are admitted byte layouts, not full-serving qualification of every combination. Backend/model reachability follows upstream main; this change does not enable combinations absent from its native loader. Compact UE8M0 scales expand losslessly for the FP32 API image; arbitrary FP32 scales and conversion fallbacks are rejected. CuTe wrappers/derived buffers must already exist. Supported architectures are `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`. Attention TP/CP/DCP=1, PP=1, expert TP=1, fixed expert topology and the Python server with one tokenizer worker are required; no LoRA, disaggregation, EPLB, redundant experts or elastic joins.

For TRTLLM NVFP4 with clamped activation, gate/up global scales must remain tied. Admission rejects an untied starting image, and preparation rejects an update that would require block-scale requantization; this path never requantizes weights. Physical weight and block-scale row order follows the ordinary loader, while global scalar halves retain canonical gate/up order.

For MXFP4 on upstream main, TRTLLM and MegaMoE use the transformed live images in `w13_weight_scale_inv` / `w2_weight_scale_inv`; the TRTLLM clamp tensor belongs to the quantization method. GPU-delta binds and tracks those existing consumers. Layout preparation remains separate from the unchanged DE/Triton apply path, with no update-time weight conversion.

## Accuracy Tests

### Source and environment

- **Source:** base `e152f531d9553906aa421c85da290d55c6e9492c`; candidate `1b4879231e96311248a12dd070c0da0327ad3288`. Three commits keep the implementation (`8169d3c8ca64a53ecc5bd59997119dcb0e94dc0e`), NVFP4 compatibility (`8c8a60337fd7a53b0cc34dece823cb0dd256ffe9`) and main MXFP4 consumer ownership (`1b4879231e96311248a12dd070c0da0327ad3288`) reviewable separately.
- **Hardware:** C3 `hu-wtc-107`, eight NVIDIA B300 SXM6 GPUs (SM10.3), driver 595.91.07, 256 logical CPUs.
- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261102-38d9e4a3`; manifest digest `sha256:77ff63ee69fd7ebef20df3a6d036ee4b8a4ffe0734efb0028c3b7643386e3ccf`; amd64 digest `sha256:c6da252c6837bb062184b01c7aa2df7a2aadb1ed4944f236d7027174c73c45fa`.
- **Runtime:** Python 3.12.16 at `/opt/sglang/bin/python3`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, pytest 9.2.0, Zstandard 0.25.0 and LZ4 4.4.5. Missing-only setup added nvCOMP 5.3.0.16, python-snappy 0.7.3 and cramjam 2.11.0 with `--no-deps --only-binary=:all:`; all other installed distributions were unchanged.
- **Source binding:** complete manifest SHA256 `6f3124a4581c9ca5e7d708c7899257886f3e7d542e1775f5fbb0bb8cdcea21a9`; actual SGLang/Miles import paths are checked against the frozen source. The paired Miles tree is `efa7ea5a1f21138f92eb110e33f20fe6123d5515`; its tests are not part of this native run.

### Native validation

**C3 PASS: 210 tests + 62 subtests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips (111.08 s).** The wrapper passed; all 15,780 source files remained unchanged, the original test processes exited and GPUs were idle afterward.

The SGLang registered GPU-delta suite and four manual CUDA/DE files cover API/session boundaries, canonical layout agreement with ordinary loader helpers, exact-byte apply/status gates, host-cache reuse and allocator/stream ownership. Normal conftest and the image's native dependencies are used. Counts below are from this completed C3 run. **Boundaries:** paired Miles API tests were not run. The stock SGLang image has no Ray, and Miles conftest eagerly imports its rollout stack; trainer/Ray dependencies were not installed for unchanged Miles code. SGLang API tests exercise the request contracts. No model-serving, separate eval-engine E2E, full-model final-weight oracle, RL run or concurrent-serving-interference validation is claimed.

### Reproduction

For the same fresh image, install only these three missing packages:

```bash
/opt/sglang/bin/python3 -m pip install --no-deps --only-binary=:all: \
  nvidia-libnvcomp-cu13==5.3.0.16 python-snappy==0.7.3 cramjam==2.11.0
```

With the paired checkout directories at the exact source revisions above, run the native group once. `OUT` must be a fresh writable result directory. The validation harness records stdout/stderr/JUnit, verifies the full source inventory before/after, and checks original process exit and GPU-idle state. Its direct test invocation is:

```bash
S=/absolute/path/to/paired-checkouts
OUT=/absolute/path/to/fresh/test-output
mkdir "$OUT"
unset GPU_DELTA_SKIP_PAYLOAD_HASH PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export PYTHONPATH="$S/sglang/python:$S/miles" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export GPU_DELTA_CPU_WORKERS=32 GPU_DELTA_LAYERS_PER_BATCH=1 GPU_DELTA_SORT_BEFORE_HW_DECOMPRESS=0
export SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_SCHEDULER=0
cd "$S/sglang"
/opt/sglang/bin/python3 -B -m pytest -o addopts= -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  --junitxml="$OUT/sglang-gpu-delta.xml" \
  test/registered/unit/gpu_delta_weight_sync \
  test/manual/gpu_delta/test_codec.py \
  test/manual/gpu_delta/test_host_cuda.py \
  test/manual/gpu_delta/test_apply_cuda.py \
  test/manual/gpu_delta/test_device_allocator_cuda.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A benchmark was not requested and was not run for this upstream-main source on C3. [The counterpart PR's validation section](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42210) records historical receiver benchmarks on its own source, image and C2 node; those timings are not new-main performance evidence or a no-regression claim. No Nsight capture was run here.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Apply canonical Miles deltas directly to live SGLang weights, including HF-base recovery on fresh engines. This targets upstream `main`; the `sglang-miles` counterpart is [SGLang #42210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42210), paired with [Miles #3894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3894).

## Modifications

- **Lifecycle/API:** `/get_gpu_delta_info`, `/update_weights_from_gpu_delta`, `/get_gpu_delta_status` and `/clear_gpu_delta_state` serve the Miles client. One update carries the negotiated participants/session and publication descriptor, then owns preparation, pause/fence/apply, all-rank acknowledgement and resume. Failed preparation is released; uncertain XOR application is never replayed. Model labels become visible before generation resumes.
- **Preparation:** validate manifests, read/hash into shared tmpfs, decode/copy into private rank HOST_NUMA arenas, and prepare byte descriptors and three fixed access-family kernels. Bulk byte copies release the GIL. Private scalar patches use empty storage for full replacement or a clone for partial replacement, with batched copies. Cache one decode-status kernel per device. Live weight writes wait for pause; concurrent-serving impact has not been measured. `GPU_DELTA_HOST_CACHE_DIR` must name host-shared tmpfs when overridden.
- **Apply/storage:** one hardware-DE stream, one Triton stream and exactly two decoded slots, ordered by decode-ready/apply-finished events. Sticky status guards subsequent mutation. DE-facing allocations own their CUDA storage; streams drain before release on failure/cancellation. No pipeline-depth tuning, runtime autotuning or encoded-HBM ring.
- **Integrity/recovery:** `validate_payload_hash=True` is the sole receiver hash-policy input; disabling it skips payload SHA passes only. Manifest/file/native checks remain. Ordinary updates use consecutive transport versions; fresh engines can accept HF base→current. State stays cached unless cleared explicitly or via `release_state=True` after successful resume. Cleanup does not change weights/version/pause timing; caller-owned pauses are preserved.
- **Observability:** retain rank/engine phase metrics for Miles/W&B without added collective, polling or device synchronization. Standard `SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1` marks host preparation, scheduler and worker/enqueue ranges; the benchmark controls capture. Disabled tracing leaves callables unchanged.

### Compatibility

Blackwell hardware DE; no software-decompression fallback or weight requantization. Admission maps existing FlashInfer packed buffers into canonical affine byte views; padding is excluded, aliases receive one XOR, and independently owned consumer images each receive it. There is no update-time weight/mask permutation.

| Weight format | FlashInfer TRTLLM family | CuTe DSL | MegaMoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | Yes | — | — |
| FP8 128×128, UE8M0 scales | Yes | — | — |
| MXFP8 | Yes | — | Yes |
| MXFP4 × MXFP8 activation | Yes | — | Yes |
| NVFP4 | W4A4 | W4A4 / W4A16 | W4A4 / W4A16 |

These are admitted byte layouts, not full-serving qualification of every combination. Backend/model reachability follows upstream main; this change does not enable combinations absent from its native loader. Compact UE8M0 scales expand losslessly for the FP32 API image; arbitrary FP32 scales and conversion fallbacks are rejected. CuTe wrappers/derived buffers must already exist. Supported architectures are `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`. Attention TP/CP/DCP=1, PP=1, expert TP=1, fixed expert topology and the Python server with one tokenizer worker are required; no LoRA, disaggregation, EPLB, redundant experts or elastic joins.

For TRTLLM NVFP4 with clamped activation, gate/up global scales must remain tied. Admission rejects an untied starting image, and preparation rejects an update that would require block-scale requantization; this path never requantizes weights. Physical weight and block-scale row order follows the ordinary loader, while global scalar halves retain canonical gate/up order.

For MXFP4 on upstream main, TRTLLM and MegaMoE use the transformed live images in `w13_weight_scale_inv` / `w2_weight_scale_inv`; the TRTLLM clamp tensor belongs to the quantization method. GPU-delta binds and tracks those existing consumers. Layout preparation remains separate from the unchanged DE/Triton apply path, with no update-time weight conversion.

## Accuracy Tests

### Source and environment

- **Source:** base `e152f531d9553906aa421c85da290d55c6e9492c`; candidate `1b4879231e96311248a12dd070c0da0327ad3288`. Three commits keep the implementation (`8169d3c8ca64a53ecc5bd59997119dcb0e94dc0e`), NVFP4 compatibility (`8c8a60337fd7a53b0cc34dece823cb0dd256ffe9`) and main MXFP4 consumer ownership (`1b4879231e96311248a12dd070c0da0327ad3288`) reviewable separately.
- **Hardware:** C3 `hu-wtc-107`, eight NVIDIA B300 SXM6 GPUs (SM10.3), driver 595.91.07, 256 logical CPUs.
- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261102-38d9e4a3`; manifest digest `sha256:77ff63ee69fd7ebef20df3a6d036ee4b8a4ffe0734efb0028c3b7643386e3ccf`; amd64 digest `sha256:c6da252c6837bb062184b01c7aa2df7a2aadb1ed4944f236d7027174c73c45fa`.
- **Runtime:** Python 3.12.16 at `/opt/sglang/bin/python3`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, pytest 9.2.0, Zstandard 0.25.0 and LZ4 4.4.5. Missing-only setup added nvCOMP 5.3.0.16, python-snappy 0.7.3 and cramjam 2.11.0 with `--no-deps --only-binary=:all:`; all other installed distributions were unchanged.
- **Source binding:** complete manifest SHA256 `6f3124a4581c9ca5e7d708c7899257886f3e7d542e1775f5fbb0bb8cdcea21a9`; actual SGLang/Miles import paths are checked against the frozen source. The paired Miles tree is `efa7ea5a1f21138f92eb110e33f20fe6123d5515`; its tests are not part of this native run.

### Native validation

**C3 PASS: 210 tests + 62 subtests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips (111.08 s).** The wrapper passed; all 15,780 source files remained unchanged, the original test processes exited and GPUs were idle afterward.

The SGLang registered GPU-delta suite and four manual CUDA/DE files cover API/session boundaries, canonical layout agreement with ordinary loader helpers, exact-byte apply/status gates, host-cache reuse and allocator/stream ownership. Normal conftest and the image's native dependencies are used. Counts below are from this completed C3 run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling

A benchmark was not requested and was not run for this upstream-main source on C3. [The counterpart PR's validation section](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42210) records historical receiver benchmarks on its own source, image and C2 node; those timings are not new-main performance evidence or a no-regression claim. No Nsight capture was run here.

+
+"""Prepared groups of byte-affine XOR destinations; imported only at admission."""
+
+import math
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from functools import lru_cache, partial
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+BLOCK = 2048
+ELEMENTS = 512
+WARPS = 4
+RESIDENT_WAVES = 4
+MAX_AXES = 64
+_INT64_MAX = (1 << 63) - 1
+_MAX_TILES = (1 << 31) - 1
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None, typed=True)
+def _resident_ctas(kernel, device_index):
+    """One resource-residency wave, cached per loaded kernel and CUDA device."""
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index):
+        status, blocks = driver.cuOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(
+            driver.CUfunction(int(kernel.function)),
+            kernel.metadata.num_warps * 32,
+            kernel.metadata.shared,
+        )
+        if status != driver.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS or blocks <= 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"CUDA occupancy query failed: status={status}, blocks={blocks}"
+            )
+        return (
+            blocks
+            * torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device_index).multi_processor_count
+        )
+
+
+@triton.jit(
+    do_not_specialize=["count"],
+    do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[
+        "statuses",
+        "actual_sizes",
+        "expected_sizes",
+        "count",
+    ],
+)
+def _check_decode(
+    statuses, actual_sizes, expected_sizes, error, count, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
+):
+    index = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    active = index < count
+    status = tl.load(statuses + index, active, other=0)
+    actual = tl.load(actual_sizes + index, active, other=0)
+    expected = tl.load(expected_sizes + index, active, other=0)
+    if tl.sum(((status != 0) | (actual != expected)).to(tl.int32), 0) != 0:
+        tl.atomic_or(error, 1)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None, typed=True)
+def _compiled_status(device_index):
+    """Load one status kernel per device; frame counts remain runtime values."""
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index):
+        kernel = _check_decode.warmup(
+            torch.int32,
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int32,
+            0,
+            1024,
+            grid=(1, 1, 1),
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+        _ = kernel.run
+        return kernel
+
+
+def prepare_status_check(decoder, error):
+    """Prepare metadata-only validation; the returned call enqueues on apply."""
+    count = decoder.statuses.numel()
+    arguments = (
+        decoder.statuses,
+        decoder.actual_sizes,
+        decoder.expected_sizes,
+        error,
+        count,
+    )
+    grid = (triton.cdiv(count, 1024), 1, 1)
+    kernel = _compiled_status(decoder.statuses.device.index)
+    return partial(kernel[grid], *arguments)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _scalar_quotient(numerator, denominator):
+    # Runtime scalar row/base division: never narrow a large coordinate or axis.
+    if numerator <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
+        if denominator > 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            quotient = tl.full((), 0, tl.int64)
+        else:
+            quotient = (numerator.to(tl.uint32) // denominator.to(tl.uint32)).to(
+                tl.int64
+            )
+    else:
+        quotient = numerator // denominator
+    return quotient
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _affine_offset(index, metadata, shape, stride, axes):
+    offset = tl.full(index.shape, 0, tl.int64)
+    rest = index
+    axis = axes - 1
+    while axis > 0:
+        length = tl.load(metadata + shape + axis)
+        step = tl.load(metadata + stride + axis)
+        quotient = _scalar_quotient(rest, length)
+        offset += (rest - quotient * length) * step
+        rest = quotient
+        axis -= 1
+    return offset + rest * tl.load(metadata + stride)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _affine_lanes(base, delta, metadata, shape, stride, axes, MAX_DELTA: tl.constexpr):
+    offset = tl.full(delta.shape, 0, tl.int64)
+    axis = axes - 1
+    while axis > 0:
+        length = tl.load(metadata + shape + axis)
+        step = tl.load(metadata + stride + axis)
+        quotient = _scalar_quotient(base, length)
+        remainder = base - quotient * length
+        if length > MAX_DELTA:
+            lane_quotient = tl.full(delta.shape, 0, tl.uint32)
+            lane_remainder = delta
+        else:
+            lane_quotient = delta // length.to(tl.uint32)
+            lane_remainder = delta - lane_quotient * length.to(tl.uint32)
+        # b=qL+r, d=aL+t => coordinate=r+t-cL, next flat=q+a+c.
+        # 0<=t<L gives a single carry; the new delta a+c never exceeds d.
+        # Group subtraction before addition to avoid an overflowing r+t when
+        # a valid axis approaches INT64_MAX. Only bounded deltas use uint32.
+        carry = (lane_remainder.to(tl.int64) >= length - remainder).to(tl.uint32)
+        coordinate = remainder + (
+            lane_remainder.to(tl.int64) - carry.to(tl.int64) * length
+        )
+        offset += coordinate * step
+        base = quotient
+        delta = lane_quotient + carry
+        axis -= 1
+    return offset + (base + delta.to(tl.int64)) * tl.load(metadata + stride)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _load_source(
+    source,
+    metadata,
+    shape,
+    axes,
+    mode,
+    base,
+    size,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+    index = base + lanes * WORD
+    mask = index < size
+    # Keep the actual memory operations in the uniform access-mode branches.
+    # Merging an arbitrary affine offset before a common load loses the
+    # contiguous branch's vector-address proof. Only base has a fixed multiple;
+    # arbitrary outer strides in row/affine mappings keep their true alignment.
+    if mode == 1:
+        offset = tl.multiple_of(base // WORD, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+        value = tl.load(source + offset, mask, other=0)
+    elif PACKED or mode == 2:
+        if PACKED:
+            start = _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, ELEMENTS * WORD)
+        else:
+            start = _affine_offset(base, metadata, shape, shape + axes, axes)
+        start = tl.multiple_of(start // WORD, ALIGNMENT // WORD)
+        value = tl.load(source + start + lanes, mask, other=0)
+    else:
+        offset = _affine_lanes(
+            base,
+            (lanes * WORD).to(tl.uint32),
+            metadata,
+            shape,
+            shape + axes,
+            axes,
+            (ELEMENTS - 1) * WORD,
+        )
+        value = tl.load(source + offset // WORD, mask, other=0)
+    return value
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _xor_target(
+    target,
+    value,
+    metadata,
+    shape,
+    axes,
+    mode,
+    base,
+    size,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+    index = base + lanes * WORD
+    mask = index < size
+    if mode == 1:
+        offset = tl.multiple_of(base // WORD, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+    elif PACKED or mode == 2:
+        if PACKED:
+            start = _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, ELEMENTS * WORD)
+        else:
+            start = _affine_offset(base, metadata, shape, shape + axes, axes)
+        start = tl.multiple_of(start // WORD, ALIGNMENT // WORD)
+        offset = start + lanes
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+    else:
+        offset = (
+            _affine_lanes(
+                base,
+                (lanes * WORD).to(tl.uint32),
+                metadata,
+                shape,
+                shape + axes,
+                axes,
+                (ELEMENTS - 1) * WORD,
+            )
+            // WORD
+        )
+        previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+        tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _packed_row_start(base, metadata, shape, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    # Packed row contracts are exactly two axes; contiguous sides bypass this.
+    # Active total tiles <= INT32_MAX and the inner row is BLOCK-divisible.
+    # Keep only tile division uint32; byte coordinates/strides remain int64.
+    inner = tl.load(metadata + shape + 1)
+    outer_stride = tl.load(metadata + shape + 2)
+    tile = (base // BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    row_tiles = (inner // BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    row = (tile // row_tiles).to(tl.int64)
+    return row * outer_stride + (base - row * inner)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _apply_record(
+    pointers,
+    metadata,
+    record,
+    tile,
+    tile_stride,
+    WORD: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNMENT: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    FAMILY: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    size = tl.load(metadata + record)
+    source_mode = tl.load(metadata + record + 1)
+    target_mode = tl.load(metadata + record + 2)
+    count = tl.load(metadata + record + 6)
+    position = tl.load(metadata + record + 7)
+    first = tl.load(metadata + record + 8)
+    end = tl.load(metadata + record + 9)
+    axes = tl.load(metadata + record + 10)
+    # Active contracts have at most INT32_MAX tiles by admission. Only byte
+    # offsets/affine coordinates need int64; variable tile division uses uint32.
+    per_item = tl.cdiv(size, BLOCK).to(tl.uint32)
+    DTYPE: tl.constexpr = tl.uint32 if WORD == 4 else tl.uint8
+    ELEMENTS: tl.constexpr = 512
+    # A CTA may visit several tiles of this group. Keep record selection and
+    # scalar geometry outside that loop, then search again only across END.
+    while tile < end:
+        local = (tile - first).to(tl.uint32)
+        item = local // per_item
+        base = (local - item * per_item).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK
+        source = tl.multiple_of(tl.load(pointers + position + item), ALIGNMENT).to(
+            tl.pointer_type(DTYPE)
+        )
+        target = tl.multiple_of(
+            tl.load(pointers + position + count + item), ALIGNMENT
+        ).to(tl.pointer_type(DTYPE))
+        shape = record + 11
+        if FAMILY == 1:
+            # This family's coordinate descriptors are uint32-word based.
+            # CPU preparation validates/classifies the original byte contract;
+            # size/tile accounting stays byte-based. The source is contiguous.
+            lanes = tl.arange(0, ELEMENTS)
+            index = tl.multiple_of(base // 4, ELEMENTS) + lanes
+            target_shape = shape + 2 * axes
+            offset = _affine_lanes(
+                base // 4,
+                lanes.to(tl.uint32),
+                metadata,
+                target_shape,
+                target_shape + axes,
+                axes,
+                ELEMENTS - 1,
+            )
+            mask = base + lanes * 4 < size
+            value = tl.load(source + index, mask, other=0)
+            previous = tl.load(target + offset, mask, other=0)
+            tl.store(target + offset, value ^ previous, mask)
+        else:
+            # Keep loads/stores inside their uniform access-mode branches:
+            # merging row starts first loses the contiguous address proof.
+            # Packed WORD4 uses one subtile; general byte fallback uses four.
+            part = 0
+            while part < 4 // WORD:
+                subbase = base + part * ELEMENTS * WORD
+                value = _load_source(
+                    source,
+                    metadata,
+                    shape,
+                    axes,
+                    source_mode,
+                    subbase,
+                    size,
+                    WORD,
+                    ELEMENTS,
+                    ALIGNMENT,
+                    FAMILY == 0,
+                )
+                _xor_target(
+                    target,
+                    value,
+                    metadata,
+                    shape + 2 * axes,
+                    axes,
+                    target_mode,
+                    subbase,
+                    size,
+                    WORD,
+                    ELEMENTS,
+                    ALIGNMENT,
+                    FAMILY == 0,
+                )
+                part += 1
+        tile += tile_stride
+    return tile
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _xor_batch(pointers, metadata, error, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, FAMILY: tl.constexpr):
+    # No pointer or model access may precede the sticky decode-status gate.
+    if tl.load(error) == 0:
+        tile = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        tile_stride = tl.num_programs(0).to(tl.int64)
+        groups = tl.load(metadata)
+        total = tl.load(metadata + groups)  # final END; metadata[0] is0 if empty
+        while tile < total:
+            low = tl.full((), 0, tl.int64)
+            high = groups
+            # First cumulative END greater than tile. Empty groups are skipped.
+            while low < high:
+                middle = (low + high) // 2
+                end = tl.load(metadata + 1 + middle)
+                if tile < end:
+                    high = middle
+                else:
+                    low = middle + 1
+            record = tl.load(metadata + 1 + groups + low)
+            word = tl.load(metadata + record + 5)
+            if FAMILY != 2 or word == 4:
+                source_alignment = tl.load(metadata + record + 3)
+                target_alignment = tl.load(metadata + record + 4)
+                if (source_alignment >= 16) & (target_alignment >= 16):
+                    tile = _apply_record(
+                        pointers,
+                        metadata,
+                        record,
+                        tile,
+                        tile_stride,
+                        4,
+                        16,
+                        BLOCK,
+                        FAMILY,
+                    )
+                else:
+                    tile = _apply_record(
+                        pointers,
+                        metadata,
+                        record,
+                        tile,
+                        tile_stride,
+                        4,
+                        4,
+                        BLOCK,
+                        FAMILY,
+                    )
+            else:
+                tile = _apply_record(
+                    pointers, metadata, record, tile, tile_stride, 1, 1, BLOCK, FAMILY
+                )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None, typed=True)
+def _compiled(device_index, family):
+    """Three fixed access families per device, all loaded before pause."""
+    if (
+        type(device_index) is not int
+        or not 0 <= device_index < torch.cuda.device_count()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply device")
+    if type(family) is not int or family not in (0, 1, 2):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply family")
+    with torch.cuda.device(device_index):
+        kernel = _xor_batch.warmup(
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int64,
+            torch.int32,
+            BLOCK,
+            family,
+            grid=(1, 1, 1),
+            num_warps=WARPS,
+        )
+        _ = kernel.run
+        _resident_ctas(kernel, device_index)
+        return kernel
+
+
+def _normalize(shape, stride):
+    """Keep the same flat element mapping with fewer affine axes."""
+    axes = []
+    for size, step in reversed(tuple(zip(shape, stride))):
+        if size == 1:
+            continue
+        if axes and step == axes[-1][0] * axes[-1][1]:
+            axes[-1] = (size * axes[-1][0], axes[-1][1])
+        else:
+            axes.append((size, step))
+    if not axes:
+        return (1,), (1,)
+    shape, stride = zip(*reversed(axes))
+    return shape, stride
+
+
+def _access_mode(shape, stride, block):
+    """Classify normalized byte geometry without model or format dimensions.
+
+    0: arbitrary affine coordinates; each lane computes its runtime byte offset.
+    1: contiguous bytes; flat logical and physical offsets are identical.
+    2: contiguous innermost rows whose lengths are block-divisible, so a tile
+       cannot cross a row boundary; only the tile's row start needs remapping.
+    """
+    if stride == (1,):
+        return 1
+    return 2 if stride[-1] == 1 and shape[-1] % block == 0 else 0
+
+
+def _word_bytes(contract, alignment):
+    size, ss, st, ts, tt = contract
+    aligned_rows = all(
+        stride[-1] == 1
+        and shape[-1] % 4 == 0
+        and all(n == 1 or step % 4 == 0 for n, step in zip(shape[:-1], stride[:-1]))
+        for shape, stride in ((ss, st), (ts, tt))
+    )
+    return 4 if size % 4 == 0 and min(alignment) >= 4 and aligned_rows else 1
+
+
+def _row_alignment(shape, stride, alignment):
+    if _access_mode(shape, stride, BLOCK) != 2:
+        return alignment
+    # The inner row coordinate is BLOCK aligned. Include every active outer
+    # stride so a16B base pointer never overstates a4B-aligned row start.
+    return math.gcd(
+        alignment, *(step for n, step in zip(shape[:-1], stride[:-1]) if n > 1)
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_contract(contract, count):
+    size, ss, st, ts, tt = contract
+    if (
+        type(count) is not int
+        or not 0 <= count <= _INT64_MAX
+        or type(size) is not int
+        or not 0 < size <= _INT64_MAX
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply size/count")
+    for shape, stride in ((ss, st), (ts, tt)):
+        if not 1 <= len(shape) <= MAX_AXES or len(shape) != len(stride):
+            raise ValueError("unsupported GPU delta affine axis count")
+        if any(type(n) is not int or not 0 < n <= _INT64_MAX for n in shape) or any(
+            type(step) is not int or not 0 <= step <= _INT64_MAX for step in stride
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta affine geometry")
+        if (
+            math.prod(shape) != size
+            or sum((n - 1) * step for n, step in zip(shape, stride)) > _INT64_MAX
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta affine extent")
+    if count * triton.cdiv(size, BLOCK) > _INT64_MAX:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta apply tile count overflow")
+
+
+def _record(contract, count, alignment, position):
+    """Prepare one record from its original byte contract and pointer position.
+
+    Classify once in byte units. Only word-affine coordinate descriptors are then
+    normalized into uint32-word units; size/count/tile fields remain byte-based.
+    """
+    _validate_contract(contract, count)
+    if len(alignment) != 2 or any(a not in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) for a in alignment):
+        raise ValueError("invalid GPU delta apply pointer alignment")
+    if type(position) is not int or not 0 <= position <= _INT64_MAX - 2 * count:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta apply pointer position overflow")
+    size, ss, st, ts, tt = contract
+    source_mode = _access_mode(ss, st, BLOCK)
+    target_mode = _access_mode(ts, tt, BLOCK)
+    alignment = (
+        _row_alignment(ss, st, alignment[0]),
+        _row_alignment(ts, tt, alignment[1]),
+    )
+    word = _word_bytes(contract, alignment)
+    if (
+        word == 4
+        and source_mode in (1, 2)
+        and target_mode in (1, 2)
+        and (source_mode == 1 or len(ss) == 2)
+        and (target_mode == 1 or len(ts) == 2)
+    ):
+        family = 0
+    elif word == 4 and source_mode == 1:
+        family = 1
+        # Discard inactive axes before dividing potentially arbitrary strides.
+        # WORD4 admission proves divisibility of every active outer stride and
+        # the contiguous inner length. A four-byte inner axis becomes unit.
+        ts, tt = _normalize(ts, tt)
+        ts, tt = _normalize(
+            (*ts[:-1], ts[-1] // 4),
+            (*(step // 4 for step in tt[:-1]), 1),
+        )
+        ss, st = (size // 4,), (1,)
+    else:
+        family = 2
+    axes = max(len(ss), len(ts))
+    values = [
+        size,
+        source_mode,
+        target_mode,
+        *alignment,
+        word,
+        count,
+        position,
+        0,
+        0,
+        axes,
+    ]
+    for shape, stride in ((ss, st), (ts, tt)):
+        values.extend((*shape, *((1,) * (axes - len(shape)))))
+        values.extend((*stride, *((0,) * (axes - len(stride)))))
+    return family, tuple(values)
+
+
+def _metadata(records):
+    """Assemble one family's END/index header and records, padded to 16 bytes."""
+    values = [len(records)] + [0] * (2 * len(records))
+    first = 0
+    for index, record in enumerate(records):
+        end = first + record[6] * triton.cdiv(record[0], BLOCK)
+        if end > _MAX_TILES:
+            raise ValueError("GPU delta apply metadata overflow")
+        values[1 + index] = end
+        values[1 + len(records) + index] = len(values)
+        values.extend((*record[:8], first, end, *record[10:]))
+        first = end
+    # Preserve the precompiled pointer signature for the next slab slice.
+    if len(values) % 2:
+        values.append(0)
+    return values, first
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApplyProgram:
+    family: str
+    kernel: object
+    metadata_start: int
+    metadata_stop: int
+    tiles: int
+    grid: tuple
+    resident_ctas: int
+
+
+def _launch_prebound(calls):
+    for call in calls:
+        call()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ByteApplyGroup:
+    """A runtime batch partitioned into three fixed, prewarmed access families."""
+
+    sources: list[int]
+    targets: list[int]
+    contracts: tuple
+    kernels: tuple = ()
+    _prepared_device: int | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
+
+    def prepare_metadata(self, device_index):

+"""Canonical metadata for the GPU-delta receiver's immutable startup checkpoint.
+
+Read only at first delta admission. The exclusive controller must keep the
+original local checkpoint unchanged for the engine's lifetime; this is metadata
+discovery, not proof of the current model's weight values. Ordinary loaders and
+model methods are never modified.
+"""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from safetensors import safe_open
+
+
+def read_canonical_checkpoint_inventory(model_runner):
+    """Read source names, shapes and dtypes without materializing any tensors.
+
+    The source inventory is independent of quantization. Runtime layout admission
+    checks the physical buffers and model mappings separately.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import DefaultModelLoader, ModelOptModelLoader
+    from sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils import (
+        filter_duplicate_safetensors_files,
+        maybe_add_mtp_safetensors,
+    )
+
+    model = model_runner.model
+    config = model_runner.load_config
+    model_config = model_runner.model_config
+    loader = model_runner.loader
+    # ModelOpt's already-quantized branch delegates to DefaultModelLoader.
+    # Subclasses may override the iterator or transform its names and values.
+    if type(loader) not in (DefaultModelLoader, ModelOptModelLoader):
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires the standard local checkpoint loader")
+    if type(loader) is ModelOptModelLoader and not model_config._is_already_quantized():
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support load-time ModelOpt conversion")
+    if config.load_format not in {"auto", "safetensors", "fastsafetensors"}:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires a standard safetensors load format")
+    if model_runner.is_draft_worker or config.draft_model_idx is not None:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta checkpoint admission requires the target model")
+    if (
+        getattr(model, "secondary_weights", ())
+        or getattr(model, "allow_patterns_overrides", None) is not None
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support secondary or remapped sources")
+    if config.decryption_key_file is not None:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta does not support encrypted checkpoint sources")
+
+    folder = Path(model_config.model_path)
+    if not folder.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta requires the original immutable local checkpoint")
+    # Match the default loader's primary source (empty prefix, no draft remap).
+    # Reuse its index filtering and bundled-MTP rules without invoking downloads,
+    # checksum verification, tensor loading, or checkpoint page-cache prefetch.
+    files = filter_duplicate_safetensors_files(
+        [str(path) for path in folder.glob("*.safetensors")],
+        str(folder),
+        "model.safetensors.index.json",
+    )
+    files = maybe_add_mtp_safetensors(
+        files, str(folder), "model.safetensors.index.json", model_config.hf_config
+    )
+    if not files:
+        raise ValueError("GPU delta checkpoint has no selected safetensors shards")
+    return _read_headers(files)
+
+
+def _read_headers(files):
+    inventory = {}
+    for path in files:
+        with safe_open(path, framework="pt", device="cpu") as source:
+            for name in source.keys():  # noqa: SIM118 - safe_open is not iterable.
+                if name in inventory:
+                    raise ValueError(f"ambiguous canonical checkpoint tensor: {name}")
+                tensor_slice = source.get_slice(name)
+                inventory[name] = {
+                    "shape": tensor_slice.get_shape(),
+                    "dtype": tensor_slice.get_dtype(),
+                }
+    if not inventory:
+        raise ValueError("canonical checkpoint metadata is empty")
+    return inventory

+"""Caller-owned nvCOMP decoding for direct weight deltas.
+
+Preparation allocates small metadata and workspace; decoded output slots are bound
+only after generation pauses.
+The hot path calls the public C API directly: no nvCOMP Python array finalizers,
+implicit size discovery, host scalar reads or wrapper-added synchronization.
+The nvCOMP DE backend may wait for earlier work on the calling stream before
+submitting decompression, even though the public API is named Async.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+import importlib.metadata
+import os
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta import profiling
+
+
+class _SnappyOptions(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("backend", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("sort_before_hw_decompress", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("reserved", ctypes.c_char * 56),
+    ]
+
+
+class _Lz4Options(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("backend", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("sort_before_hw_decompress", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("data_type", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("bitshuffle_mode", ctypes.c_int),
+        ("reserved", ctypes.c_char * 48),
+    ]
+
+
+_DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS = {
+    "snappy": ("Snappy", _SnappyOptions),
+    "lz4": ("LZ4", _Lz4Options),
+}
+_MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 4 << 20
+_INT64_MAX = np.iinfo(np.int64).max
+
+
+def _require_hardware_device(device: torch.device, algorithm: str) -> int:
+    from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import _driver
+
+    driver = _driver()
+    status, mask = driver.cuDeviceGetAttribute(
+        driver.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_MASK,
+        device.index,
+    )
+    if status:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU-delta DE device admission failed: CUDA {status}")
+    status, maximum = driver.cuDeviceGetAttribute(
+        driver.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_DECOMPRESS_MAXIMUM_LENGTH,
+        device.index,
+    )
+    if status:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU-delta DE device admission failed: CUDA {status}")
+    algorithms = driver.CUmemDecompressAlgorithm
+    required = {
+        "Snappy": algorithms.CU_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_SNAPPY,
+        "LZ4": algorithms.CU_MEM_DECOMPRESS_ALGORITHM_LZ4,
+    }[algorithm]
+    if not mask & required:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Device has no hardware {algorithm} decompressor")
+    if maximum <= 0:
+        raise RuntimeError("Device has no positive hardware decompression limit")
+    return maximum
+
+
+class _Alignments(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("input", ctypes.c_size_t),
+        ("output", ctypes.c_size_t),
+        ("temp", ctypes.c_size_t),
+    ]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DecodeWorkspace:
+    temporary: torch.Tensor
+    actual_sizes: torch.Tensor
+    statuses: torch.Tensor
+
+
+class NvcompDecoder:
+    """One device's fixed inner-codec hardware decoder.
+
+    Missing libraries and unsupported hardware fail admission. There is no CPU
+    decoder, algorithm substitution or software fallback.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, device: torch.device, inner_codec: str):
+        self.device = torch.device(device)
+        if self.device.type != "cuda" or self.device.index is None:
+            raise ValueError("Delta decoder requires an explicit CUDA device")
+        if inner_codec not in _DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS:
+            raise ValueError("GPU delta inner codec must be snappy or lz4")
+        self.inner_codec = inner_codec
+        self._algorithm, options_type = _DECOMPRESS_OPTIONS[inner_codec]
+        sorting = os.environ.get("GPU_DELTA_SORT_BEFORE_HW_DECOMPRESS", "0")
+        if sorting not in {"0", "1"}:
+            raise ValueError("GPU_DELTA_SORT_BEFORE_HW_DECOMPRESS must be 0 or 1")
+        cuda_major = torch.version.cuda.split(".")[0]
+        package = f"nvidia-libnvcomp-cu{cuda_major}"
+        distribution = importlib.metadata.distribution(package)
+        version = tuple(int(v) for v in distribution.version.split(".")[:2])
+        if not (5, 3) <= version < (6, 0) or ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_size_t) != 8:
+            raise RuntimeError("Direct GPU deltas require the 64-bit nvCOMP 5.3+ ABI")
+        self.backend = "hardware"
+        self._options = options_type()
+        # Explicit backend selection: DEFAULT can silently select software.
+        self._options.backend = 1
+        self._options.sort_before_hw_decompress = int(sorting)
+        if self._algorithm == "LZ4":
+            self._options.data_type = 0  # NVCOMP_TYPE_CHAR
+            self._options.bitshuffle_mode = 0  # NVCOMP_BITSHUFFLE_NONE
+        self.maximum_chunk_bytes = _require_hardware_device(
+            self.device, self._algorithm
+        )
+        self._library = ctypes.CDLL(
+            str(distribution.locate_file("nvidia/libnvcomp/lib64/libnvcomp.so.5"))
+        )
+        pointer, size = ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t
+        self._temporary = self._bind(
+            "GetTempSizeAsync", [size, size, options_type, ctypes.POINTER(size), size]
+        )
+        required_alignments = self._bind(
+            "GetRequiredAlignments", [options_type, ctypes.POINTER(_Alignments)]
+        )
+        self._decode = self._bind(
+            "Async",
+            [
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+                size,
+                pointer,
+                size,
+                pointer,
+                options_type,
+                pointer,
+                pointer,
+            ],
+        )
+        self.alignments = _Alignments()
+        self._check(required_alignments(self._options, ctypes.byref(self.alignments)))
+        self._temporary_sizes: dict[tuple[int, int, int], int] = {}
+
+    def _bind(self, suffix, arguments):
+        function = getattr(
+            self._library,
+            "nvcompBatched" + self._algorithm + "Decompress" + suffix,
+        )
+        function.argtypes, function.restype = arguments, ctypes.c_int
+        return function
+
+    def _check(self, status):
+        if status != 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"nvCOMP {self.inner_codec}/{self.backend} failed: status={status}"
+            )
+
+    def temporary_bytes(self, geometry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> int:
+        if not geometry[0]:
+            return 0
+        cached = self._temporary_sizes.get(geometry)
+        if cached is not None:
+            return cached
+        size = ctypes.c_size_t()
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device):
+            self._check(
+                self._temporary(
+                    geometry[0],
+                    geometry[1],
+                    self._options,
+                    ctypes.byref(size),
+                    geometry[2],
+                )
+            )
+        self._temporary_sizes[geometry] = size.value
+        return size.value
+
+    def _allocate_workspace(self, geometry) -> DecodeWorkspace:
+        """One DE stream shares scratch; statuses/sizes belong to two slots."""
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import device_empty
+
+        maximum_count = max((batch[0] for batch in geometry), default=0)
+        temporary = max((self.temporary_bytes(batch) for batch in geometry), default=0)
+        workspace = DecodeWorkspace(
+            device_empty((temporary,), dtype=torch.uint8, device=self.device),
+            device_empty((2, maximum_count), dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device),
+            device_empty((2, maximum_count), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device),
+        )
+        if temporary and workspace.temporary.data_ptr() % self.alignments.temp:
+            raise ValueError("Misaligned decoder workspace")
+        return workspace
+
+    def _frame_geometry(self, table, counts, input_base, input_bytes):
+        """Validate numeric rows and derive workspace/output bounds in one pass."""
+        if (
+            table.dtype != np.int64
+            or table.shape != (4, sum(counts))
+            or not table.flags.c_contiguous
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Expected contiguous int64(4,N) frame metadata")
+        if not 0 <= input_base <= _INT64_MAX - input_bytes:
+            raise ValueError("Input pointer arithmetic exceeds signed metadata")
+        bounds, remainders, geometry = [0, 0], [None, None], []
+        maximum = self.maximum_chunk_bytes
+        offset = 0
+        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
+            inputs, encoded, decoded, outputs = table[:, offset : offset + count]
+            offset += count
+            slot = index % 2
+            if not count:
+                geometry.append((0, 0, 0))
+                continue
+            # HARDWARE does not check oversized buffers. Check actual lengths,
+            # not the compressor's worst-case allocation: compressible 4 MiB
+            # frames can fit the device limit.
+            if (
+                np.any(decoded <= 0)
+                or np.any(decoded > min(_MAX_FRAME_BYTES, maximum))
+                or np.any(encoded <= 0)
+                or np.any(encoded > maximum)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "GPU-delta frames require positive lengths, <=4 MiB "
+                    f"output and both lengths <= device limit {maximum}"
+                )
+            if np.any(inputs < 0) or np.any(inputs > input_bytes - encoded):
+                raise ValueError("Encoded frame outside input allocation")
+            if np.any(outputs < 0) or np.any(outputs > _INT64_MAX - decoded):
+                raise ValueError("Output arithmetic exceeds signed metadata")
+            if np.any(outputs[1:] < outputs[:-1] + decoded[:-1]):
+                raise ValueError("Overlapping or unordered decoded frames")
+            if np.any((inputs + input_base) % self.alignments.input):
+                raise ValueError("Misaligned encoded frame")
+            remainder = outputs % self.alignments.output
+            first = int(remainder[0])
+            if np.any(remainder != first) or remainders[slot] not in (None, first):
+                raise ValueError("Misaligned decoded frame")
+            remainders[slot] = first
+            bounds[slot] = max(bounds[slot], int(outputs[-1] + decoded[-1]))
+            if count > _INT64_MAX // maximum:
+                raise ValueError("Decoded geometry sum exceeds signed metadata")
+            geometry.append((count, int(decoded.max()), int(decoded.sum())))
+        return geometry, bounds, remainders
+
+    @profiling.annotate("gpu_delta.prepare.decoder_metadata")
+    def prepare_batches(
+        self,
+        table: np.ndarray,
+        counts: Sequence[int],
+        host_input: torch.Tensor,
+        stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
+    ) -> PreparedDecodePlan:
+        """Prepare numeric metadata and small workspace without decoded output.
+
+        Rows contain relative input offsets, encoded sizes, decoded sizes and
+        relative output offsets. The admitted host arena must stay immutable
+        until the DE stream drains. Only input/size rows are uploaded now;
+        ``bind_outputs`` fills output pointers under the serving pause.
+        """
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import device_empty
+
+        if (
+            host_input.device.type != "cpu"
+            or host_input.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or not host_input.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("nvCOMP input must be a contiguous host arena byte view")
+        if stream.device != self.device:
+            raise ValueError("Decoder stream/device mismatch")
+        input_base = host_input.data_ptr()
+        geometry, bounds, remainders = self._frame_geometry(
+            table, counts, input_base, host_input.numel()
+        )
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.device), torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            workspace = self._allocate_workspace(geometry)
+            host = torch.empty(
+                table.shape, dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu", pin_memory=True
+            )
+            host_rows = host.numpy()
+            np.add(table[0], input_base, out=host_rows[0])
+            host_rows[1:3] = table[1:3]
+            metadata = device_empty(host.shape, dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
+            if metadata.numel():
+                metadata[:3].copy_(host[:3], non_blocking=True)
+        return PreparedDecodePlan(
+            self,
+            counts,
+            host_input,
+            workspace,
+            host,
+            metadata,
+            stream,
+            table[3].copy(),
+            bounds,
+            remainders,
+        )
+
+
+class PreparedDecodePlan:
+    """Publication metadata and output leases, bound only while paused."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        decoder,
+        counts,
+        host_input,
+        workspace,
+        host_metadata,
+        metadata,
+        stream,
+        output_offsets,
+        output_bounds,
+        output_remainders,
+    ):
+        self.decoder, self.stream = decoder, stream
+        self.workspace = workspace
+        self.host_metadata, self.metadata = host_metadata, metadata
+        self.output_bounds, self.output_remainders = output_bounds, output_remainders
+        # Every batch retains this same list. Binding fills it only after all
+        # output checks pass; dropping the plan alone cannot free in-flight slots.
+        self.decoded_slots = []
+        self.batches = []
+        temporary = workspace.temporary
+        offset = 0
+        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
+            slot = index % 2
+            rows = metadata[:, offset : offset + count]
+            host_rows = host_metadata[:, offset : offset + count]
+            statuses = workspace.statuses[slot, :count]
+            actual_sizes = workspace.actual_sizes[slot, :count]
+            expected_sizes = rows[2]
+            arguments = (
+                rows[0].data_ptr(),
+                rows[1].data_ptr(),
+                expected_sizes.data_ptr(),
+                actual_sizes.data_ptr(),
+                count,
+                temporary.data_ptr(),
+                temporary.numel(),
+                rows[3].data_ptr(),
+                decoder._options,
+                statuses.data_ptr(),
+                stream.cuda_stream,
+            )
+            self.batches.append(
+                PreparedDecode(
+                    decoder,
+                    host_input,
+                    self.decoded_slots,
+                    workspace,
+                    host_rows,
+                    rows,
+                    stream,
+                    statuses,
+                    actual_sizes,
+                    expected_sizes,
+                    arguments,
+                    output_offsets[offset : offset + count],
+                    host_rows[3].numpy(),
+                )
+            )
+            offset += count
+        self.record_stream(stream)
+
+    def record_stream(self, stream):
+        """Register every consumer before it can enqueue storage readers."""
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import record_device_stream
+
+        if stream.device != self.decoder.device:
+            raise ValueError("Decoder consumer stream/device mismatch")
+        for tensor in (
+            self.metadata,
+            self.workspace.temporary,
+            self.workspace.actual_sizes,
+            self.workspace.statuses,
+            *self.decoded_slots,
+        ):
+            record_device_stream(tensor, stream)
+
+    @profiling.annotate("gpu_delta.pause.bind_decoder_outputs")
+    def bind_outputs(
+        self, decoded_slots: Sequence[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> list[PreparedDecode]:
+        """Check paused allocations, fill output pointers, upload just row 3.
+
+        Slot bounds and relative pointer alignment were computed during prepare.
+        The caller waits for prior apply readers before reusing each output and
+        its status/actual-size row. Temporary storage is reused on the DE stream.
+        """
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.memory import (
+            record_device_stream,
+            require_de_capable,
+        )
+
+        if len(decoded_slots) != 2:
+            raise ValueError("Decoded output count differs from prepared slots")
+        for tensor in decoded_slots:
+            if (
+                tensor.device != self.decoder.device
+                or tensor.dtype != torch.uint8
+                or not tensor.is_contiguous()
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "nvCOMP outputs must be contiguous bytes on the decoder device"
+                )
+        bases = [tensor.data_ptr() for tensor in decoded_slots]
+        capacities = [tensor.numel() for tensor in decoded_slots]
+        if (
+            capacities[0]
+            and capacities[1]
+            and bases[0] < bases[1] + capacities[1]
+            and bases[1] < bases[0] + capacities[0]
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Decoded output slots must not overlap")
+        for base, capacity, bound, remainder in zip(
+            bases, capacities, self.output_bounds, self.output_remainders
+        ):
+            if capacity < bound:
+                raise ValueError("Out-of-bounds decoded frame")
+            if (
+                remainder is not None
+                and (base + remainder) % self.decoder.alignments.output
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("Misaligned decoded frame")
+        for tensor in decoded_slots:
+            record_device_stream(tensor, self.stream)
+        with torch.cuda.device(self.decoder.device), torch.cuda.stream(self.stream):
+            for base, capacity in zip(bases, capacities):
+                if capacity:
+                    require_de_capable(base)
+            for index, batch in enumerate(self.batches):
+                np.add(
+                    batch.output_offsets,
+                    bases[index % 2],
+                    out=batch.output_pointers,
+                )
+            if self.metadata.numel():
+                self.metadata[3].copy_(self.host_metadata[3], non_blocking=True)
+        self.decoded_slots[:] = decoded_slots
+        return self.batches
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PreparedDecode:
+    decoder: NvcompDecoder
+    host_input: torch.Tensor
+    decoded_slots: list[torch.Tensor]
+    workspace: DecodeWorkspace
+    host_metadata: torch.Tensor
+    metadata: torch.Tensor
+    stream: torch.cuda.Stream
+    statuses: torch.Tensor
+    actual_sizes: torch.Tensor
+    expected_sizes: torch.Tensor
+    _arguments: tuple
+    output_offsets: np.ndarray
+    output_pointers: np.ndarray
+
+    @profiling.annotate("gpu_delta.pause.nvcomp_enqueue")
+    def enqueue(self) -> None:
+        """Launch only; caller checks statuses/sizes on device before applying weights.
+
+        This object and all storage must outlive the submitted work. There is no
+        normal-path synchronization here; the session owns the final fence and
+        enters the captured DE stream/device context around submission. Foreign
+        allocation finalizers also fence their recorded consumers before freeing.
+        """
+        if not self.statuses.numel():
+            return
+        self.decoder._check(self.decoder._decode(*self._arguments))

+"""FlashInfer expert layouts expressed as views of live consumer bytes.

+The apply kernel knows only affine byte coordinates. These admission-time

+    # gated groups, then TRTLLM's 32-row transpose (4 x 8 -> 8 x 4).
+    if group:
+        row = row // group * (2 * group) + half * group + row % group

+        row = row // 32 * 32 + row % 4 * 8 + row % 32 // 4
+    return row

+def _factored_segments(
+    images,
+    rows,
+    cols,
+    element_size,
+    row_offset,
+    column_block,
+    column_stride,
+    block_stride,
+):
+    """Factor fixed row-bit permutations into affine axes, excluding padding.
+
+    A 128-row bulk plus binary tail pieces gives at most eight row rectangles.
+    Columns need at most a full-block rectangle and one tail. No tensor data,
+    index tensor, or weight-sized intermediate is constructed.
+    """
+    byte_cols = cols * element_size
+    full = byte_cols // column_block * column_block
+    columns = [(0, full)] if full else []
+    if full < byte_cols:
+        columns.append((full, byte_cols))
+    images = tuple(_bytes(image) for image in _unique_images(images))
+    result = []
+    for r0, r1, unit in _row_pieces(rows):
+        bits = [1 << bit for bit in reversed(range(unit.bit_length() - 1))]
+        shape = ((r1 - r0) // unit, *(2 for _ in bits))
+        origin = row_offset(r0)
+        strides = (
+            row_offset(r0 + unit) - origin,
+            *(row_offset(r0 + bit) - origin for bit in bits),
+        )
+        for c0, c1 in columns:
+            if (c1 - c0) % column_block == 0:
+                cshape = ((c1 - c0) // column_block, column_block)
+                cstrides = (block_stride, column_stride)
+            else:
+                cshape, cstrides = (c1 - c0,), (column_stride,)
+            offset = origin + c0 // column_block * block_stride
+            destinations = tuple(
+                image.as_strided(
+                    (*shape, *cshape),
+                    (*strides, *cstrides),
+                    image.storage_offset() + offset,
+                )
+                for image in images
+            )
+            result.append(
+                DestinationSegment(
+                    ((r0, r1), (c0 // element_size, c1 // element_size)), destinations
+                )
+            )
+    return tuple(result)

+def _scale_parameter(layer, stem, layout):

+            suffix = "weight_scale"

+        if layout.format == "nvfp4":
+            suffix = "weight_scale"

+def _weight_image(layer, stem, expert, layout):
+    image = getattr(layer, f"{stem}_weight")[expert]

+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported TRTLLM weight format: {layout.format}")

+        if layout.format == "nvfp4":

+        if layout.format == "nvfp4":
+            # NVFP4 retains the transpose as a view; recover physical packed rows.
+            image = image.transpose(0, 1)

+        elif layout.format == "mxfp8":
+            # MXFP8 materializes the transpose; its physical rows are K-major.
+            rows, cols = image.shape[1], image.shape[0]
+        elif layout.format == "mxfp4":
+            rows, cols = image.shape[0], image.shape[1]
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported MegaMoE weight format: {layout.format}")
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported FlashInfer expert backend: {layout.backend}")

+def _mapping(layout, projection):
+    if layout.backend == "trtllm":
+        if layout.format in {"bf16", "nvfp4", "mxfp4", "mxfp8"}:
+            group, shuffle = 1, True
+        elif layout.format == "fp8-block128-ue8m0":

+            group, shuffle = 0, False

+            group, shuffle = 64, False

+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported CuTe DSL expert format: {layout.format}")
+    elif layout.backend == "megamoe":
+        if layout.format == "nvfp4":
+            # NVFP4 MegaMoE: Gate16, Up16, Gate16, Up16, ...
+            group, shuffle = 16, False
+        elif layout.format == "mxfp8":
+            group, shuffle = 32, False
+        elif layout.format == "mxfp4":
+            group, shuffle = 8, False
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported MegaMoE expert format: {layout.format}")
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported FlashInfer expert backend: {layout.backend}")

+        group, half = 0, 0
+    else:
+        half = int((projection == "up") != layout.up_first)

+def expert_scale_target(layer, layout, local_expert, projection, canonical_shape):
+    """Existing FP32 API storage for lossless block-128 UE8M0 expansion.
+
+    The binding prepares complete FP32 values separately; XOR byte views cannot
+    express the change of representation from an exponent byte to FP32.
+    """
+    if layout.format != "fp8-block128-ue8m0" or layout.backend != "trtllm":
+        raise ValueError("FP32 scale target requires native block-128 UE8M0")

+        projection not in {"gate", "up", "down"}
+        or (projection == "gate" and not layout.gated)
+        or len(canonical_shape) != 2
+        or any(type(n) is not int or n <= 0 for n in canonical_shape)
+        or type(local_expert) is not int
+        or local_expert < 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid block-128 scale projection")

+    target = getattr(layer, f"{stem}_weight_scale_inv")[local_expert]
+    if target.dtype != torch.float32 or target.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError("unexpected block-128 FP32 scale image")
+    rows, cols = canonical_shape
+    if layout.gated and projection != "down":
+        if target.shape[0] % 2:
+            raise ValueError("invalid block-128 gate/up scale geometry")
+        half_rows = target.shape[0] // 2
+        start = half_rows if projection == "up" else 0
+        if rows > half_rows:
+            raise ValueError("block-128 scale projection exceeds its half")
+        target = target[start : start + rows]
+    if rows > target.shape[0] or cols > target.shape[1]:
+        raise ValueError("block-128 scale projection exceeds live storage")
+    return target[:rows, :cols]

+"""Feature-owned HTTP and IPC schemas for GPU-delta controls."""
+
+from typing import Any, Dict, List
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import BaseReq, hook_custom_types
+
+
+class ClearGpuDeltaStateReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    pass
+
+
+class ReleaseGpuDeltaCacheReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    # Internal second phase, sent only after every rank has closed its resources.
+    owner_rank_ids: List[str]
+
+
+class GetGpuDeltaInfoReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    engine_id: str
+
+
+class PrepareGpuDeltaReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    session_id: str
+    manifest_path: str
+    manifest_sha256: str
+    stream_id: str
+    base_version: int
+    target_version: int
+    plan_digest: str
+    participants: List[Dict[str, Any]]
+    validate_payload_hash: bool = True
+
+
+class UpdateWeightsFromGpuDeltaReqInput(PrepareGpuDeltaReqInput, kw_only=True):
+    release_state: bool = False
+    flush_cache: bool = True
+    abort_all_requests: bool = False
+    weight_version: str | None = None
+
+
+class GetGpuDeltaStatusReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    session_id: str
+
+
+class ApplyGpuDeltaReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    session_id: str
+    flush_cache: bool = True
+    abort_all_requests: bool = False
+
+
+class AbortGpuDeltaReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    session_id: str
+
+
+class ResumeGpuDeltaReqInput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    session_id: str
+    keep_pause: bool = False
+    weight_version: str | None = None
+
+
+class GpuDeltaReqOutput(BaseReq, kw_only=True):
+    success: bool
+    message: str
+    participant: Dict[str, Any]
+
+
+# Register before tokenizer/scheduler/DP-controller receive loops start.
+hook_custom_types(
+    UpdateWeightsFromGpuDeltaReqInput,
+    ClearGpuDeltaStateReqInput,
+    ReleaseGpuDeltaCacheReqInput,
+    GetGpuDeltaInfoReqInput,
+    PrepareGpuDeltaReqInput,
+    GetGpuDeltaStatusReqInput,
+    ApplyGpuDeltaReqInput,
+    AbortGpuDeltaReqInput,
+    ResumeGpuDeltaReqInput,
+    GpuDeltaReqOutput,
+)

+"""Immutable canonical layout admission and live-consumer identity checks."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from itertools import chain
+
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta import profiling
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.bindings import (
+    BACKEND_LAYOUTS,
+    ConsumerSnapshot,
+    _digest,
+    _tensor_identity,
+)
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.derived import nvfp4_derived_update, plan_updates
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.flashinfer import consumer_objects
+from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.models import model_mapping
+
+
+class GpuDeltaLayout:
+    """Frozen canonical bindings with generic backend and consumer admission."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model, inventory):
+        from sglang.srt.weight_sync.gpu_delta.host import _natural_key
+
+        if not inventory:
+            raise ValueError("canonical checkpoint metadata is unavailable")
+        # Normalize negotiated wire metadata without changing checkpoint inventory.
+        self.inventory = {name: dict(meta) for name, meta in inventory.items()}
+        mapping = model_mapping(model)
+        self.bindings = []
+        self.excluded = mapping.parameters.excluded
+        for name, meta in self.inventory.items():
+            binding = mapping.bind(name, meta)
+            if binding is not None:
+                self.bindings.append(binding)
+        self.bindings.sort(key=lambda b: _natural_key(b.name))
+        if mapping.parameters.moe_layers:
+            from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+
+            _require_fixed_moe_topology(get_exec().moe)
+        self.derived = []
+        self.derived_updates = []
+        self._consumers = []
+        for prefix, layer in mapping.parameters.moe_layers.items():
+            layout = mapping.parameters.moe_layouts[prefix]
+            if layout.format == "nvfp4":
+                self.derived_updates.append(
+                    nvfp4_derived_update(layer, layout.backend, layout.quant_mode)
+                )
+            self._consumers.append(
+                ConsumerSnapshot(
+                    lambda layer=layer, layout=layout: consumer_objects(layer, layout)
+                )
+            )
+        self.derived_updates = plan_updates(
+            self.derived_updates,
+            [
+                target
+                for binding in self.bindings
+                if binding.encoding == "raw_bytes"
+                for target in binding.storage
+            ],
+        )
+        mapping.finish()
+        self.derived.extend(mapping.derived)
+        self._consumers.extend(mapping.consumers)
+        self._parameter_roots = [
+            (module, name, tensor, _tensor_identity(tensor))
+            for module in mapping.parameters.modules.values()
+            for name, tensor in module._parameters.items()
+            if tensor is not None
+        ]
+        self._prepare_identity_checks()
+        self._reject_overlaps(mapping.aliases)
+        self.description = {
+            "layouts": dict(BACKEND_LAYOUTS),
+            "tensors": [b.describe() for b in self.bindings],
+            "excluded": self.excluded,
+        }
+        self.rank_plan_digest = _digest(self.description)
+        self.description["rank_plan_digest"] = self.rank_plan_digest
+
+    def _prepare_identity_checks(self):
+        # Deduplicate geometry once, not in the per-update validation loop.
+        # Separate views sharing storage still require separate geometry checks.
+        checks = chain(
+            (
+                (tensor, expected, "parameter identity")
+                for _, _, tensor, expected in self._parameter_roots
+            ),
+            (
+                (consumer.objects[index], expected, "consumer storage")
+                for consumer in self._consumers
+                for index, expected in consumer.tensors
+            ),
+        )
+        unique = {}
+        for tensor, expected, kind in checks:
+            key = id(tensor)
+            prior = unique.get(key)
+            if prior is None:
+                unique[key] = (tensor, expected, kind)
+            elif prior[1] != expected:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"GPU delta {kind} changed during admission; readmission required"
+                )
+        self._tensor_checks = tuple(unique.values())
+
+    @profiling.annotate("gpu_delta.check_identity")
+    def check_identity(self):
+        for module, name, tensor, _ in self._parameter_roots:
+            if module._parameters.get(name) is not tensor:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    "GPU delta parameter identity changed; readmission required"
+                )
+        for consumer in self._consumers:
+            consumer.check_objects()
+        for tensor, expected, kind in self._tensor_checks:
+            if _tensor_identity(tensor) != expected:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"GPU delta {kind} changed; readmission required")
+
+    def _reject_overlaps(self, model_aliases):
+        # Gate/up intentionally share one interleaved weight/scale allocation;
+        # their maps are disjoint. Other shared storage needs an explicit alias
+        # adapter so a tied parameter is never XORed twice.
+        owners = {}
+        for binding in self.bindings:
+            for tensor in binding.storage:
+                key = tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+                prior = owners.get(key)
+                if prior and prior != binding.name:
+                    pair = (prior, binding.name)
+                    if not all(".experts." in name for name in pair) and not (
+                        _gate_up_alias(*pair) or model_aliases(*pair)
+                    ):
+                        raise ValueError(f"unclassified live weight alias: {pair}")
+                owners[key] = binding.name
+
+
+def _gate_up_alias(a, b):
+    return (
+        a.replace("gate_proj", "up_proj") == b or b.replace("gate_proj", "up_proj") == a
+    )
+
+
+def _require_fixed_moe_topology(moe):
+    # The canonical expert map is valid only while physical expert ownership is
+    # the trivial EP partition. EPLB/custom/elastic maps can change ownership
+    # without changing tensor pointers, so pointer checks alone cannot admit it.
+    if (
+        moe.enable_eplb
+        or moe.elastic_ep_backend is not None
+        or moe.init_expert_location != "trivial"
+        or moe.ep_num_redundant_experts != 0
+        or (moe.moe_runner_backend, moe.moe_a2a_backend)
+        not in {
+            ("flashinfer_trtllm", "none"),
+            ("flashinfer_trtllm_routed", "none"),
+            ("flashinfer_mxfp4", "none"),
+            ("flashinfer_cutedsl", "none"),
+            ("flashinfer_megamoe", "flashinfer_megamoe"),
+        }
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "direct GPU deltas require fixed trivial EP, no redundant experts or EPLB, "
+            "and a native FlashInfer runner with its matching dispatcher"
+        )
